findings.title: Record editor open + prefill (create path, result.state === 'none')
findings.detail:
openRecordEditor (src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:1464-1522) is the only place the editor opens (pencil tap, wired at line 3533: `onclick={() => openRecordEditor(row)}`). It resets `recordEditorLookup = null`, `recordEditorOriginal = null` (line 1474), and `recordForm = { name: '', phone: '', email: '', birthdate: '', id_code: '' }` (line 1475) BEFORE the async lookup settles. On `result.state === 'none'` (lines 1484-1497) it prefills:
```
recordForm = {
    name: row.profileName ?? row.name,
    phone: '',
    email: row.email,
    birthdate: '',
    id_code: ''
};
```
So on first open (no record yet): `name` and `email` are prefilled non-empty from the profile/row; `phone`, `birthdate`, `id_code` open blank. `recordEditorOriginal` stays `null` on this branch — it is set only in the `result.state === 'one'` branch (line 1511: `recordEditorOriginal = { ...recordForm }`, after prefilling from the existing record at lines 1501-1510). Comment at 1484-1488 confirms intent: 'First open, no record yet (R4) — prefill from the ROW... name/email from the roster's own resolution, phone/date of birth start empty.'

findings.title: recordEditorOriginal — declaration, setter, and null-on-create-turned-update confirmed
findings.detail: Declared at lines 1430-1436 as `{ name; phone; email; birthdate; id_code } | null`, initialized to `null`. Its doc comment (1425-1429) states it is 'Read at save time only, never drives a render... null on the lazy-create path (no baseline to diff against — every save there is a create).' It is set to `{ ...recordForm }` ONLY inside the `result.state === 'one'` branch of `openRecordEditor` (line 1511) — i.e. only when a record already existed at open time. It is explicitly nulled in `openRecordEditor` (1474), in `cancelRecordEditor` (1531), and after a successful save (1694). On the create-turned-update path — editor opened when `loadMemberRecord` returned `state: 'none'` (so `recordEditorOriginal` was never set, stays null from line 1474), but the save-time fresh re-read (`saveRecordEditor`, line 1637) finds `fresh.state === 'one' \| 'damaged'` (record was created by someone else in between) — `recordEditorOriginal` IS null, confirmed. The save handler's own code (line 1674) falls back to an all-empty baseline when it is null: `const original = recordEditorOriginal ?? { name: '', phone: '', email: '', birthdate: '', id_code: '' };` This is exactly the bug issue #280 describes: the empty fallback baseline can't distinguish 'admin typed this' from 'this arrived via prefill'.

findings.title: Save handler quoted in full — fresh.state !== 'none' branch, diff computation, fields sent
No existing touched/dirty tracking anywhere in the editor — would be new
findings.detail: Searched the whole file for 'touched'/'dirty' (case-sensitive and via grep) — every hit is either an unrelated comment about other code paths ('leaves the tree untouched', 'children untouched', etc.) or the save-handler's own prose describing outcomes, never a piece of state. There is no boolean flag, Set, or per-field marker recording whether the admin edited a given input. The editor's only per-field state is `recordForm` itself (declared 1372-1384, a plain `$state<{name,phone,email,birthdate,id_code}>` object) and, when a record pre-existed at open time, `recordEditorOriginal` as the load-time snapshot. Each field input uses a bare two-way `bind:value={recordForm.<field>}` (verified at lines 3564, 3574, 3585, 3597, 3607 for name/phone/email/birthdate/id_code respectively) — nothing intercepts input events to flip a dirty flag. So implementing #280's fix (excluding untouched-but-prefilled fields from the create-turned-update diff) requires NEW per-field touched tracking; nothing to wire into exists today.

findings.title: Every field the editor manages, and prefill status of each
findings.detail: The editor manages exactly five fields, per the `recordForm` type (1372-1384) and the `RECORD_FIELD_LABEL` lookup table (1438-1444): `name`, `phone`, `email`, `birthdate`, `id_code`. Prefill behavior on first open (`result.state === 'none'`, lines 1489-1497): `name` — prefilled from `row.profileName ?? row.name` (non-empty, profile-derived). `email` — prefilled from `row.email` (non-empty, profile-derived). `phone` — opens empty (`''`); comment: 'the profile holds neither' (referring to phone/birthdate). `birthdate` — opens empty (`''`), same reason. `id_code` — opens empty (`''`); comment at 1494-1496 explicitly notes 'no prefill: nothing to prefill from, the profile layer has no such field.' So the bug's scope is exactly the two profile-sourced fields (`name`, `email`); the other three (`phone`, `birthdate`, `id_code`) are never silently non-empty on open and are already covered correctly by the existing 'diff against empty baseline' logic issue #280's own text confirms ('a field the admin left empty never overwrites a value this editor never saw' — true for those three, false for the two prefilled ones).

findings.title: The write function and wire shape
findings.detail: saveRecordEditor (src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:1548-1724) performs the save. It re-reads the record fresh at save time (loadMemberRecord, line 1637) and branches: fresh.state === 'none' -> createMemberRecord (line 1657, full non-empty input); otherwise (both create-turned-update and the normal update path go through the `else` starting at line 1666) -> a diff is built (lines 1674-1688) against `original` (recordEditorOriginal, or an all-empty fallback object at 1674-1680 when null), producing a `changes` object containing only fields whose current form value !== the baseline, then updateMemberRecord(cfg, fresh.record._id, changes) (line 1689). Wire shape: updateMemberRecord (src/lib/roster/memberRecord.ts:216-262) is property-level, NOT an atomic full-entity overwrite -- it walks FIELD_ORDER (name->phone->email->birthdate->id_code) and for each field literally present as a key in `changes` (`if (!(field in changes)) continue;`, memberRecord.ts:224) calls replaceEntityProperty (src/lib/entu/replaceProperty.ts:60-80ish) which does its own GET-then-POST-with-old-_id atomic overwrite of that ONE named property only (module header comments, replaceProperty.ts:7-21, confirm the entity POST body carries only the single prop entry). A field never added as a key to `changes` is therefore never sent in any POST and is left completely untouched server-side. So 'don't send it' (omit the key from the diff/changes object) IS sufficient to leave a field alone; no field is ever cleared by omission. Unit-confirmed at src/lib/roster/memberRecord.spec.ts:214-231: calling updateMemberRecord with only {email, name} yields exactly 2 replaceEntityProperty calls (never phone/birthdate/id_code).

findings.title: The bug's exact location
findings.detail: The bug is in the diff baseline, not the write layer. recordEditorOriginal is populated only when the editor opens with the lookup already showing state:'one' (+page.svelte:1498-1511). On the create-turned-update path -- editor opened while state was 'none' (prefilled from row.name/row.email, lines 1489-1497), and by save time a fresh lookup finds state:'one' (someone else created the record meanwhile) -- recordEditorOriginal is still null, so the fallback all-empty baseline is used (lines 1674-1680). Diffing form values against an EMPTY baseline means the untouched prefilled name/email (non-empty strings the admin never edited) count as 'changed' and ARE included in `changes`, so they get sent via updateMemberRecord and silently overwrite whatever the other writer already saved into those two fields. The code's own comment at lines 1669-1673 states the (incorrect) guarantee that this is safe.

findings.title: Specs covering the record editor / create-turned-update / #268 save-time existence check
findings.detail: All in src/routes/page.roster-record-editor.spec.ts (component-level: `// @vitest-environment happy-dom` pragma at line 1, `@testing-library/svelte` render of the actual route, line 38). Relevant blocks: (C) prefill, lines 386-444 -- prefill-only assertions (name=row.name/email=row.email on 'none'; record wins on 'one'), no diff assertions. (E) save, lines 465-573: lines 476-494 assert the create-path full input; lines 546-559 cover the NORMAL update path (editor opened already on state:'one', so recordEditorOriginal is a real baseline) -- asserts updateMemberRecord sent ONLY {name:'Uus Nimi'}; correct, unaffected by the bug. (E) review r3 F2, lines 927-987, is #268's save-time existence check block: lines 933-941 assert the save re-reads before writing; lines 943-968 is the create-turned-update test and it ENCODES THE CURRENT BUGGY BEHAVIOUR -- it opens the editor on state:'none' (prefill fires), then makes the fresh save-time lookup return state:'one' with a different existing record, and asserts (lines 959-962) `updateMemberRecordMock.mock.calls[0][2]).toEqual({ name: 'Berta Bass', email: 'berta@example.com' })` -- i.e. it currently REQUIRES the untouched prefilled name+email be sent as 'changes'. Its own comment (956-958) states the guarantee that is wrong for non-empty prefills. This test will need its expectation rewritten (e.g. to `{}`) once the fix tracks touched-ness. Lines 970-987 cover the damaged-at-save-time branch, unaffected by this bug (no diff involved). src/lib/roster/memberRecord.spec.ts only unit-tests memberRecord.ts given an already-built `changes` object and never constructs the page-level diff, so it cannot encode this bug either way.

findings.title: Existing spec already drives two overlapping writers
findings.detail: Yes -- src/routes/page.roster-record-editor.spec.ts:943-968 is the only spec that does. Its own comments (lines 930, 947) name the scenario explicitly: 'a retry after an ambiguous create failure, or a second admin saving the same pre-record member' / '...or a second admin's save'. Mechanically: editor A's prefilled form state is held by the component while the mocked loadMemberRecord return value is swapped mid-test to simulate a record that appeared from elsewhere between open and save -- exactly the two-writer race. Grepped src/routes/*.spec.ts and src/lib/roster/*.spec.ts for 'second admin'/'two admin'/'overlap': the only other hit is an unrelated replaceEntityProperty race note at page.roster-record-editor.spec.ts:837 (a different mechanism, the property-level concurrent-replace race, not the prefill-diff bug).

findings.title: #265 and #268 commits -- what each actually changed
findings.detail: #265 (issue, CLOSED, task label) is the SCHEMA COMMISSION only: Mihkel's ruling defining the admin_member_record entity shape, per-field sharing tiers (name domain; phone/email/birthdate private), the R2 display-toggle, and the prefill-with-independence rule (R4: 'tuginedes, aga mitte sõltudes' -- seeded from profile but never live-dependent). It produced schema/migration commits only (cb43a29 'feat(schema): admin_member_record + roster_show_real_names definitions (#265)', 452dfd8 provisioning scripts, plus dry-run/live-provisioning commits through b4c7530/8b5ae8d) -- NONE touch src/routes/roster/+page.svelte or memberRecord.ts. #268 (issue, CLOSED, ready+task) is 'Admin member records: create and edit real name, phone, email, date of birth' -- its single GREEN commit is 120d7d0 'feat(#268): admin records member details in-row on the roster ...' (Mon Sep 7 09:57:20 2026), which added the entire in-row editor end to end: the pencil affordance, openRecordEditor/cancelRecordEditor/saveRecordEditor in +page.svelte, and the whole memberRecord.ts data layer (loadMemberRecord/createMemberRecord/updateMemberRecord/birthdateToWire/birthdateFromWire/MemberRecordPartialSaveError). That commit's own message point (5) already flags the prefill-source choice for PO review, and explicitly states the create-turned-update deviation as deliberate and reviewer-endorsed: 'create-turned-update sends the non-empty field set against the fresh _id ... pushing empty fields would blank a concurrent admin's freshly-created values' -- this is precisely the mechanism #280 narrows. Consequence for the fix: reuse saveRecordEditor's existing create-turned-update branch and fresh-lookup discipline as-is (it is otherwise sound, reviewer-endorsed, and #264-compliant for the damaged case); the fix is scoped to how the `original` baseline / touched-ness is tracked (lines 1674-1688) plus updating the test at page.roster-record-editor.spec.ts:943-968, not re-deriving the create-vs-update branching or the memberRecord.ts write layer.

findings.title: Runner / unit vs component
findings.detail: Single command for everything: `pnpm test` -> `vitest run` (package.json:13), one shared vitest.config.ts (mergeConfig over vite.config.ts), default environment 'node', include glob `src/**/*.spec.ts` + `scripts/**/*.spec.ts`, with global networkGuard.setup.ts blocking any real fetch. Unit vs component is per-file, not a separate runner/config: src/lib/roster/memberRecord.spec.ts carries no `@vitest-environment` pragma (runs under default 'node') and is a pure unit test of the memberRecord.ts module with resolveTypeId/replaceEntityProperty mocked -- no DOM, no Svelte rendering. src/routes/page.roster-record-editor.spec.ts opens with `// @vitest-environment happy-dom` (line 1) and uses `render`/`fireEvent`/`waitFor` from `@testing-library/svelte` (line 38) to mount the actual roster route component with its data-layer calls mocked -- genuine component-level testing of +page.svelte.

findings.title: Issue #244's gear/`seasonManageGearDisabled` references are stale — replaced by #261 rework
findings.detail:
Issue #244 (opened before #261 landed, commit b58d334) cites `season-manage-gear` at `src/routes/+page.svelte:5749` and a `seasonManageGearDisabled` variable. Neither exists at HEAD. `grep -rn seasonManageGearDisabled` and a grep for the identifier `season-manage-gear` in +page.svelte both return nothing. The #261 rework ('season card rework: + Hooaeg above, name-only collapsed card, title-row trashcan, gear removed') removed the gear entirely for everyone. Test files confirm removal, e.g. `src/routes/page.season-card.spec.ts:565` `expect(q(container, 'season-manage-gear'), 'the gear is removed').toBeNull();` and `src/lib/testing/seasonCard.ts:3` comment 'the [⚙] `season-manage-gear` ... is REMOVED'.

The successor mechanism is explicit in code comments at `src/routes/+page.svelte:4713-4712` area: 'the title-row COLLAPSE control (the gear's successor as the only close control left) ... #213 Gama ruling (1), retargeted #261'. So every place #244 says 'gear' / `seasonManageGearDisabled` now means the `season-card-collapse` button and `seasonCardCollapseDisabled` derived value respectively. This does not change the required behaviour (the same refusal condition must still be respected), but an implementation referencing the issue's literal identifiers won't match current code — worth flagging in any implementation PR so a reviewer doesn't think the issue went unread.

findings.title: (1) Panel open/collapsed state variable and its two toggle controls
findings.detail:
State variable: `let seasonManageOpen = $state(false);` — `src/routes/+page.svelte:2481`.

There is no single 'gear' any more; two separate buttons toggle it depending on current state:
- Collapsed face — opens the panel: `data-testid="season-card-expand"` button at `src/routes/+page.svelte:5704`, `onclick={openSeasonManagePanel}` at `:5708`. `openSeasonManagePanel()` (starts `:2862`) sets `seasonManageOpen = true` at `:2868`.
- Opened face — collapses the panel: `data-testid="season-card-collapse"` button at `:5763`, `onclick={closeSeasonManagePanel}` at `:5768`, gated by `disabled={seasonCardCollapseDisabled}` at `:5766`. `closeSeasonManagePanel()` (starts `:2936`) sets `seasonManageOpen = false` at `:2959`, after checking the refusal condition at `:2958`: `if (seriesRunUnfinished || eventConvertRunUnfinished) return;`.

Which face renders is driven by `{#if !seasonManageOpen}` / `{:else}` around `:5666-5668` / `:5717`.

findings.title: (2) Successor to `seasonManageGearDisabled` is `seasonCardCollapseDisabled` — exact refusal condition
(3) Event-create handler `submitEventCreate` — success/failure branches and collapse attach point
findings.detail:
Handler: `async function submitEventCreate(): Promise<void>` — `src/routes/+page.svelte:4305-4454`.

Failure branches (each sets an error and `return`s, leaving `seasonManageOpen` untouched, panel/form open with state intact): field-validation refusals at `:4326-4368` (season/type/datetime/end-before-start/name), the `resolveDatabaseEntityId` catch at `:4383-4386`, the 'no resolvable database entity' branch at `:4388-4391`, and the `createEvent` call's own catch at `:4416-4419` — each calls `setEventCreateError(...)` then `return`s before touching the panel.

Success branch begins right after `createEvent` resolves without throwing, at `:4422`: captures `origin = eventCreateOrigin`, sets success status (`:4426-4429`), `closeEventCreateForm()` (`:4430` — unmounts the create FORM, not the season-management panel), `loadForSelected({ keepSeasonManage: origin === 'panel' })` (`:4440`, explicitly keeps the panel mounted for a panel-born create), conditionally `refreshSeasonManageLists(cfg, panelSeasonId)` (`:4445-4447`), then `restoreEventCreateFocus(origin)` (`:4448`) — all with no early return in between. This is where a `closeSeasonManagePanel()` call (or a condition-respecting collapse) attaches, e.g. right after `:4448`, still inside the `try`, before the `finally` at `:4449-4452` that releases `eventCreateSubmitting`. Attaching it there guarantees it fires only on success, never on any failure `return` above.

findings.title: (4) Current focus handling on the create-success path, and existing focus helpers
Agenda row keying/testid — the scroll/highlight target
findings.detail: Rows render inside `src/lib/components/agenda/AgendaList.svelte`, not directly in `+page.svelte`. Upcoming rows: `{#each group.rows as item (item.id)}` keyed by `item.id`, testid `agenda-row-{item.id}` (AgendaList.svelte:543-544). Recent rows: `{#each recentItems as item (item.id)}`, testid `agenda-recent-row-{item.id}` (AgendaList.svelte:394,396) — this exact pattern is already used for cross-component DOM addressing, e.g. `+page.svelte:1957` builds the selector `[data-testid="agenda-recent-row-${closedItemId}"] [data-testid="take-attendance-btn"]`. So a created event's row is addressable purely via `document.querySelector('[data-testid="agenda-row-' + id + '"]')` (or the recent variant) without AgendaList exposing any new prop or element ref — `item.id` is the event entity id. `+page.svelte` passes `filteredAgendaItems` (the #214-filtered set) into `<AgendaList items={filteredAgendaItems} .../>` (+page.svelte:7717-7718): if the active filter excludes the new event's type, its row will not be in the DOM at all, so scrollIntoView would have nothing to target — this is the exact case the ruling says to surface via the toast instead of chasing with a filter write.

findings.title: #214 filter chips — state shape and why the ruling forbids writing them
findings.detail: `agendaTypeFilter` is a plain component-local `$state<AgendaTypeFilter>('all')` (+page.svelte:220-221), NOT a persisted store (unlike `$agendaViewStore`, #247's list/month toggle, which IS a persisted preference store). Reading it: `agendaFilterChips` is a `$derived.by(...)` list of types that have events (+page.svelte:233); `filteredAgendaItems` (+page.svelte:239-243) is the `$derived` filtered array actually handed to `<AgendaList>`. Writing it is mechanically a one-line assignment via `selectAgendaTypeFilter()` (+page.svelte:267-269) or direct assignment — trivially easy, which is exactly why the ruling calls it out: nothing technically stops a create-success handler from doing `agendaTypeFilter = typeValue`, but that would silently overwrite state the user set on purpose. The three EXISTING writes to `agendaTypeFilter = 'all'` (+page.svelte:277, 652, 714, plus the auto-reset `$effect` at ~262-266 when the active chip's type disappears from the season) are all legitimate resets tied to a genuine collective switch / no-agenda state / vanishing chip — none of them is 'narrow the filter to fit a new event,' confirming the create path has no precedent for touching this state and should not start one.

findings.title: No transient 'just-created' highlight pattern exists anywhere in the codebase
findings.detail: Broad search (justCreated/transient/highlight/flash/pulse-once/setTimeout-driven visual markers/keyframes) across `src/lib` and `src/routes` (excluding specs) found no timed/decaying highlight of any kind. The two nearest precedents, neither a true match: (a) `class:bg-highlight={group.relative === 'today'}` in AgendaList.svelte:515 — a STATIC condition-based class (stays highlighted as long as the condition holds; never times out), used for the 'today' day-group header, not a per-event transient marker. (b) the scroll-into-view pattern below. No shared 'flash this element then clear' utility exists to reuse — a genuinely new (small) pattern has to be built, following the nearest analog rather than reinventing scroll mechanics.

findings.title: Scroll-into-view precedent — inline component pattern, not an extracted helper
findings.detail: The only existing scrollIntoView call in the app is in `src/lib/components/attendance/AttendanceSurface.svelte:89-97`: a `panelEl = $state<HTMLDivElement|undefined>()` bound to the target div, a plain (untracked, non-`$state`) `let hasScrolled` guard, and a `$effect` that — once `loading` flips false — sets `hasScrolled = true` and does `tick().then(() => panelEl?.scrollIntoView({ block: 'start', behavior: 'smooth' }))`. There is no shared `src/lib` scroll/dom utility module (confirmed: no file matching `*scroll*`/`*dom*` outside that component's own spec) — this is a pattern to replicate inline, not a helper to import. Given the agenda row is addressable by its existing testid selector (finding 1), the created-event scroll could instead go through a plain `document.querySelector(...)?.scrollIntoView(...)` call from `+page.svelte`'s own create-success handler, without needing AttendanceSurface's bind:this machinery, since AgendaList does not expose per-row element refs to its parent.

findings.title: Created-toast surface — screen-reader-only live region, single interpolated string
findings.detail:
The only status surface on the event-create path is `
{eventCreateStatus}
` (+page.svelte:7239-7241) — visually hidden (`sr-only`), announced to assistive tech only; there is no visible toast. `eventCreateStatus` is a plain `let eventCreateStatus = $state('')` (+page.svelte:3304), set on success (+page.svelte:4426-4429) to `m.event_created({ name, when })`, a single i18n message string with no existing slot for an extra clause. Because it's a plain string assignment (not a fixed-shape typed formula), the ruling's 'say so in the created-toast' is mechanically easy: concatenate a second sentence (from a new message key) onto `eventCreateStatus` when the created event's type is not in the currently-effective filter — e.g. `eventCreateStatus = m.event_created({...}) + ' ' + m.event_created_filtered_out()`. Note: the season-create path has the exact same shape (`season-create-status`, `seasonCreateStatus`, +page.svelte:7072-7073) as an explicit sibling precedent for this kind of sr-only live-region status message. Also note: `await createEvent(cfg, input)` (+page.svelte:4415) currently DISCARDS the return value — `createEvent`'s own contract (`src/lib/entity/entityCreate.ts:492`) says it 'Resolves to the new event's entity id,' so the fix must capture that id (e.g. `const newEventId = await createEvent(cfg, input);`) to know which row to scroll/highlight and which type to check against the filter.

findings.title: i18n — message-key convention and the four bundle files
findings.detail: Convention observed in neighbouring keys is `<domain>_<subject>[_<detail>]` snake_case: `agenda_filter_all`, `agenda_filter_group_label`, `agenda_filter_empty`, `agenda_filter_recent_empty` (messages/en.json:4-7); `event_created` (messages/en.json:497, et.json:497: `"{name} loodud ajaks {when}."`); `season_created` (messages/en.json:426). New copy for this fix (the extra created-toast sentence, and/or a highlight-related aria-label if one is needed) should follow that pattern, e.g. an `event_created_filtered_out`-shaped key, added under the `event_create*`/`agenda_filter*` neighbourhood for discoverability. The four bundle paths requiring the identical new key(s) are `messages/en.json`, `messages/et.json`, `messages/lv.json`, `messages/uk.json` (confirmed present via `find`).
